title: REST API conventions
when: The user designs or cleans up an HTTP JSON API and wants consistent URLs, methods, status codes and pagination.
prompt:
Goal: Predictable resource URLs, correct methods and status codes, and uniform JSON bodies for lists, items and errors.
Steps:
1. Name resources as plural nouns: GET /api/tasks, GET /api/tasks/:id, POST /api/tasks, PATCH /api/tasks/:id, DELETE /api/tasks/:id.
2. Status codes: 200 read or update, 201 created with a Location header, 204 delete with no body, 400 invalid, 404 missing, 409 conflict, 415 wrong content type.
3. Accept and return application/json; reject other request types; limit body size.
4. Lists: ?limit=20&cursor=abc (or page) and return { items, nextCursor }; filters as query params (?status=open).
5. Use camelCase fields, ISO 8601 UTC dates and string ids; never expose internal file paths.
6. Version the path (/api/v1) once external clients depend on it.
Quality bar:
- Same shape for every list and item.
- GET never changes data.
- Unknown routes return 404 JSON.
Pitfalls:
- Verbs in URLs (/getTasks).
- 200 with an error inside the body.
- Returning all records with no limit.
Verify:
- [ ] Each route sets a status code.
- [ ] JSON responses send application/json.
- [ ] Bodies have a size limit.
- [ ] Unknown routes return 404.
Output: The routes in the server code and a short API table (method, path, body, responses) in the README.

examples.input: organize as rotas da minha API de tarefas
examples.output: GET/POST /api/tasks, PATCH/DELETE /api/tasks/:id, 201 with Location, cursor pagination
